brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three hex base pieces at (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (2,0,0) in a straight row (3 printed Hex base Full parts).

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Each cell holds one 'Bin, full depth, drained' (hex-bin-full-drain) at bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:2,0,0, filled with soil and planted (basil, chives, thyme).
Plug plants basil-young, chives-young and thyme-young sit in the three bins; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear; open faces capped and joints locked.

requirements.requirement: Drainage performance in real use (water flow, material, waterproofing)
requirements.evidence: The configurator only checks fit and collisions; it cannot verify drainage flow, PETG suitability, or waterproofing. The drained bins are the modelled drainage feature only.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full-depth hex bases in a row, each with a drained full-depth bin, soil, and a young herb plant (basil, chives, thyme). Caps on open faces and locked joints applied; check_build is clear with meshClash clear. Actual drainage and material durability are not verified by the configurator. Note that the BOM lists M6 bolts to be hand-tightened to about 2 N·m.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
